t: You're looking at numbers ten to eighteen Carlton House Terrace, a grand terrace of houses in Westminster. It was designed by John Nash, the Georgian and Regency architect responsible for many important parts of London. Nash's neoclassical and picturesque designs were financed by the Prince Regent and by the era's most successful property developer, James Burton. He also collaborated extensively with Burton's son, Decimus Burton. Stand back and take in the whole length of the terrace, which is very much in the spirit of Nash's work for the Prince Regent.
